briefing.opening: Hello everyone. August 3, 2026. As the Special Spokesperson for Climate Change, I will now begin today's climate briefing.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Heatwaves and Drought: The Normalization of Climate Crisis
sections.content: South Korea is facing an emergency situation due to consecutive days of record-breaking heatwaves. Yangsan, Gyeongnam, recorded 42.5 degrees Celsius, breaking the highest temperature ever observed, and extreme heat exceeding 40 degrees Celsius continued for five consecutive days [24, 26]. These heatwaves have now spread to the Seoul metropolitan area and western regions, with a severe heatwave warning issued for Gwangju, and a fatality presumed to be due to heatstroke occurring in Damyang, involving a person in their 70s [6, 23, 25]. Not only domestically, but the UK is also seeing its green landscapes turn brown due to relentless heatwaves [46], and Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant is at risk of shutdown due to drought [5, 45]. Water shortages are also intensifying, with drought levels elevated for the Miryang Dam on the Nakdong River and the Pyeongnim Dam on the Yeongsan River [28], clearly demonstrating that climate change is making droughts more frequent and severe [36].

sections.title: ⚠️ Ecosystem and Human Casualties: Direct Threats of Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change poses direct threats not only to human lives but also to ecosystems worldwide. The 'Red-banded Jezebel' butterfly was designated as August's endangered wild species, formalizing the threat to its survival due to climate change [1]. Internationally, large-scale wildfire damage is being reported, including two fatalities from a firefighting helicopter crash in Greece and altered wildfire paths in France [49, 50], and the U.S. has also issued warnings that wildfires will worsen if the climate crisis is ignored [31, 41]. Such climate changes can dramatically reduce water flow from western headwaters [32], and research has also been published indicating that they exacerbate inequalities in urban life [40], raising concerns about comprehensive damage.

sections.title: 🌍 The Era of Paris Agreement Implementation: Strengthening International Cooperation
sections.content: The Paris Agreement is now transitioning from the era of planning (NDCs) to implementation (BTR, Enhanced Transparency Framework) [3]. Amidst this transition, China is collaborating with the UNFCCC to support developing countries in BTR implementation, expanding its influence in the era of Paris Agreement implementation [7]. In a political context where the importance of climate change is being highlighted [34], nations are strengthening institutional and international efforts to respond to the climate crisis, including publishing reference manuals on climate change for judges [30].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Practices and Accelerated Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestically, various carbon neutrality practices and renewable energy transition efforts are accelerating to address climate change. In response to the normalization of heatwaves, the introduction of 'climate insurance' is gaining momentum [2]. A new paradigm has been presented with the nationwide expansion of 'carbon-neutral healing centers' integrating AI amidst climate change and an aging population [4]. In Gwangmyeong City, over 20,000 'Climate Volunteers' are participating in carbon neutrality practices [10], and Daejeon City has presented a blueprint for a carbon-neutral, eco-safe city through changes to its local forest plan [12]. Furthermore, efforts by corporations and local governments to transition to renewable energy are actively continuing, with Hanmi Group pursuing a 2040 RE100 roadmap [14] and Chungju City introducing additional eco-friendly hydrogen buses [13]. In Jeju, requests for the designation of a floating offshore wind demonstration complex and promises of parliamentary support have emerged [21, 22], charting the course for the renewable energy industry [15, 16, 18, 19].

sections.title: ⚠️ Shadows of the Renewable Energy Transition: Wavering Commitments and Investments
sections.content: Even amidst positive transition efforts, shadows are being cast over the process of shifting to renewable energy. News of big tech company Meta's withdrawal from RE100 raises concerns that corporate 'renewable energy commitments' may be wavering [17]. This is an issue that could significantly impact the achievement of global carbon neutrality goals. Furthermore, with solar and new renewable energy-related ETFs recording a decline in the 10% range [20], a warning light has been lit that investor sentiment in the renewable energy sector could shrink. Amidst growing calls for carbon neutrality to be achieved through action, not just reports [8], these challenges demand continuous attention and response.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has clearly illustrated the reality of the severe climate crisis, the diverse efforts being made to combat it, and the challenges in the implementation process. Climate action is no longer an option but a necessity, and sustained attention and participation from all of us are urgently required. This concludes today's climate briefing.

Yangsan, Gyeongnam, recorded a daytime high of 42.5 degrees Celsius yesterday (August 2nd), continuously breaking the highest temperature in meteorological observation history. It has exceeded 40 degrees for five consecutive days and has broken all-time highest temperature records for three consecutive days since July 31st. It is now highly probable that each summer will bring unprecedented heat.

articles.description: Water shortages are 'deepening' in the southern regions. As the drought intensifies, the drought alert levels for Milyang Dam in Yeongnam and Pyeongnim Dam in Honam have been raised. The Ministry of Climate, Energy, and Environment announced on August 2nd that Milyang Dam, a multi-purpose dam in the Nakdong River basin, entered the 'Alert' stage for drought as of midnight. Milyang Dam, located in Miryang City, Gyeongnam, supplies water to areas experiencing extreme heatwaves, including Yangsan City, Miryang City, and Changnyeong County in Gyeongnam. Drought stages include 'Attention,' 'Caution,' 'Alert,' and 'Severe.'
